history.originAnchor: A roofed house and a sound opening suggest an echo; sound borrowing later gave the meaning 'direction.'

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A roofed/house element is combined with a sound/opening element in an early graph connected with echo/resonance.
stages.stageExplanation: A roofed/house element is combined with a sound/opening element in an early graph connected with echo/resonance.
stages.transitionNote: A roofed/house element is combined with a sound/opening element in an early graph connected with echo/resonance.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Makes the roof broad and curved while the mouth becomes a clear bowl-like form inside.
stages.stageExplanation: Makes the roof broad and curved while the mouth becomes a clear bowl-like form inside.
stages.transitionNote: Makes the roof broad and curved while the mouth becomes a clear bowl-like form inside.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Straightens the roof into a tall enclosure and centers a rectangular mouth/opening sign-like element within it.
stages.stageExplanation: Straightens the roof into a tall enclosure and centers a rectangular mouth/opening sign-like element within it.
stages.transitionNote: Straightens the roof into a tall enclosure and centers a rectangular mouth/opening sign-like element within it.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Shortens and widens the enclosure, with the mouth now a compact box under the top stroke.
stages.stageExplanation: Shortens and widens the enclosure, with the mouth now a compact box under the top stroke.
stages.transitionNote: Shortens and widens the enclosure, with the mouth now a compact box under the top stroke.

recognitionTakeaway: The hand-and-cliff graph becomes 反, while reverse/return/opposition senses develop beyond the original action.
visualTeachingNotes: A hand turning back around a cliff or corner.
Oracle places a cliff-like top-and-left frame around a small hand or bent stroke, with a long arm descending outside it.
Regular 反 simplifies the cliff to 厂 and the turning hand to 又, keeping the backward-turning gesture in two compact components.

recognitionTakeaway: The crossed-body pictograph regularizes as 交 and extends to meeting, intersecting, exchanging, and interacting.
visualTeachingNotes: A standing person with the legs crossing beneath the body, shown as “meeting” or crossing.
Oracle still looks like a human figure whose lower legs cross and overlap beneath a narrow torso.
Regular 交 turns the head and body into short top strokes while preserving the decisive crossed lower lines.

history.originAnchor: A person and a reaching hand combine to show catching up; this led to 'reach.'

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A hand reaches toward and catches a person ahead, directly showing the old reaching/catching action.
stages.stageExplanation: A hand reaches toward and catches a person ahead, directly showing the old reaching/catching action.
stages.transitionNote: A hand reaches toward and catches a person ahead, directly showing the old reaching/catching action.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Simplifies the upper reach into a bold hook while several short lower strokes cluster beneath it.
stages.stageExplanation: Simplifies the upper reach into a bold hook while several short lower strokes cluster beneath it.
stages.transitionNote: Simplifies the upper reach into a bold hook while several short lower strokes cluster beneath it.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Stretches the hook into a tall enclosure-like curve with stacked horizontal contacts inside.
stages.stageExplanation: Stretches the hook into a tall enclosure-like curve with stacked horizontal contacts inside.
stages.transitionNote: Stretches the hook into a tall enclosure-like curve with stacked horizontal contacts inside.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Flattens those contacts and leaves one very long trailing stroke on the right.
stages.stageExplanation: Flattens those contacts and leaves one very long trailing stroke on the right.
stages.transitionNote: Flattens those contacts and leaves one very long trailing stroke on the right.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Condenses the entire reaching motion into three sweeping strokes, preserving the strong hook-and-catch gesture more than any literal body parts.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文

stages.transitionNote: Thickens the upper branching foot shape and gives it a long human-like lower leg.

stages.transitionNote: Formalizes the upper foot into a foot sign-like shape over two long curving legs.

history.originAnchor: A foot advances toward a marked destination. The earliest idea was movement toward a target; the later meanings ‘correct’ and ‘upright’ developed afterward.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A foot points toward a marked destination, expressing long-distance travel rather than ‘correct.’
stages.stageExplanation: A foot moves toward a destination/settlement element; this early movement/campaign graph is closely related to the word later written later campaign character.
stages.transitionNote: A foot points toward a marked destination, expressing long-distance travel rather than ‘correct.’

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Keeps the top marker detached while the lower foot becomes a compact branching shape.
stages.stageExplanation: Keeps the top marker detached while the lower foot becomes a compact branching shape.
stages.transitionNote: Keeps the top marker detached while the lower foot becomes a compact branching shape.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Joins the upper horizontal directly to a tall foot sign-like lower structure.
stages.stageExplanation: Joins the upper horizontal directly to a tall foot sign-like lower structure.
stages.transitionNote: Joins the upper horizontal directly to a tall foot sign-like lower structure.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Flattens the top line and thickens the lower foot into a compact rectangular bend.
stages.stageExplanation: Flattens the top line and thickens the lower foot into a compact rectangular bend.
stages.transitionNote: Flattens the top line and thickens the lower foot into a compact rectangular bend.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The travel sense became distinct, while the regular form came to carry the later meanings ‘correct’ and ‘upright.’
stages.stageExplanation: The structure regularizes as 正, whose familiar correct/upright senses are later than the earliest movement/campaign use.
stages.transitionNote: The travel sense became distinct, while the regular form came to carry the later meanings ‘correct’ and ‘upright.’

origin.explanation: A foot moves toward a destination or settlement marker; the early graph is connected with movement toward a target before the later “correct/upright” senses.

recognitionTakeaway: The crossroads graph regularizes as 行 and extends to going, movement, conduct, and other language-specific uses.
visualTeachingNotes: A person approaching and crossing a four-way road junction.
Oracle consists of four separate road strokes around an empty center, like a crossroads seen from above.
Regular 行 regularizes the two road-side components into the familiar left 彳-like and right strokes, preserving the sense of parallel paths and intersections.

history.originAnchor: A crossroads or road intersection originally represented a road. The later sense ‘go’ developed from movement along a road, though some analyses treat the verbal use as a sound borrowing.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Intersecting roads/crossroads form the entire picture; no person is encoded.
stages.stageExplanation: Intersecting roads/crossroads form the entire picture; no person is encoded.
stages.transitionNote: Intersecting roads/crossroads form the entire picture; no person is encoded.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Makes the crossroads even clearer with four right-angled arms meeting around the center.
stages.stageExplanation: Makes the crossroads even clearer with four right-angled arms meeting around the center.
stages.transitionNote: Makes the crossroads even clearer with four right-angled arms meeting around the center.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Separates the road into two mirrored vertical components, each with inward-curving branches.
stages.stageExplanation: Separates the road into two mirrored vertical components, each with inward-curving branches.
stages.transitionNote: Separates the road into two mirrored vertical components, each with inward-curving branches.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Keeps those mirrored road sides but shortens and thickens the branches.
stages.stageExplanation: Keeps those mirrored road sides but shortens and thickens the branches.
stages.transitionNote: Keeps those mirrored road sides but shortens and thickens the branches.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The road graph later came to mean ‘go,’ then extended to movement, conduct, and other language-specific uses.
stages.stageExplanation: The crossroads graph regularizes as 行 and extends to going, movement, conduct, and other language-specific uses.
stages.transitionNote: The road graph later came to mean ‘go,’ then extended to movement, conduct, and other language-specific uses.

recognitionTakeaway: The running graph stabilizes as 走. Japanese retains the “run” sense directly, while Mandarin later shifts strongly toward walk/go/leave.
visualTeachingNotes: A person walking forward, shown beside a path and footprint-like markers.
Oracle has a person-like upper body with legs spread over a lower crossing or foot form.
Regular 走 fixes the upper 土-like body and lower running-foot strokes into the modern character; the human figure is no longer obvious, but the movement structure remains.

recognitionTakeaway: The Chinese historical endpoint is 步; the paired-foot origin is no longer pictorial but survives in the stacked structure.
visualTeachingNotes: Two feet and a pair of footprints showing successive steps.
Oracle places two small foot-like signs one above the other, directly representing repeated stepping.
Regular 步 regularizes the upper 止-like foot and lower step strokes, preserving the idea of successive feet even after the literal prints disappear.

recognitionTakeaway: The foot pictograph stabilizes as 止 for “stop,” while 趾 later preserves the foot/toe sense.
visualTeachingNotes: A footprint and foot shown stopping, followed by a raised hand gesture for “stop.”
Oracle resembles a foot seen in profile, with a lower heel-like box and several toe or leg strokes rising above it.
Regular 止 squares the foot into vertical and horizontal strokes; the toes and heel are no longer pictorial, but their branching arrangement still underlies the form.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A hand reaches into a plant to pick; another early form shows fruit instead of the tree, so the exact original structure varies.

stages.transitionNote: A hand reaches into a plant to pick; another early form shows fruit instead of the tree, so the exact original structure varies.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文

stages.transitionNote: Enlarges the upper hand and keeps the tree below, but the fingers become short hanging marks rather than a natural hand.

stages.transitionNote: Regularizes the upper hand into several curved finger strokes over a symmetrical tree.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书

stages.transitionNote: Compresses the fingers into a small claw-like top while the tree becomes a dense tree sign-like lower component.

recognitionTakeaway: 美 preserves the stacked written result, but its ancient picture is a decorated person—not the later folk idea of “big sheep.”
visualTeachingNotes: A person wearing a large decorative headdress or plume.
Oracle shows a human body beneath an oversized branching head ornament, with the decoration dominating the figure.

Regular 美 keeps the large decorated upper section over a 大-like lower figure; the modern appearance is conventional, but the idea of an adorned person is easier to see than a literal “sheep plus big” story.

visualTeachingNotes: The sun and a crescent moon shown together.

history.originAnchor: A window and a crescent moon combine to show moonlight; this led to 'bright.'

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The selected ancient form combines light-bearing elements—here the sun and moon—to evoke dawn or brightness. Other Oracle variants use a window or eye with the moon.
stages.stageExplanation: The selected ancient form combines light-bearing elements—here the sun and moon—to evoke dawn or brightness. Other Oracle variants use a window or eye with the moon.
stages.transitionNote: The selected ancient form combines light-bearing elements—here the sun and moon—to evoke dawn or brightness. Other Oracle variants use a window or eye with the moon.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The paired elements become more regular while the two-part light structure remains clear.
stages.stageExplanation: The paired elements become more regular while the two-part light structure remains clear.
stages.transitionNote: The paired elements become more regular while the two-part light structure remains clear.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The two components are standardized into a vertically balanced written form.
stages.stageExplanation: The two components are standardized into a vertically balanced written form.
stages.transitionNote: The two components are standardized into a vertically balanced written form.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The rounded forms flatten and separate into the familiar left-and-right structure.
stages.stageExplanation: The rounded forms flatten and separate into the familiar left-and-right structure.
stages.transitionNote: The rounded forms flatten and separate into the familiar left-and-right structure.

history.originAnchor: Two separate trees stand side by side; together, they represent a forest.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Simply places two rough tree pictographs next to each other, each with branches and roots.
stages.stageExplanation: Simply places two rough tree pictographs next to each other, each with branches and roots.
stages.transitionNote: Simply places two rough tree pictographs next to each other, each with branches and roots.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文

stages.transitionNote: Keeps both trees separate but makes their trunks, branches, and roots straighter and more regular.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书

history.originAnchor: An early foot held back by a thread-like element suggests lagging behind; the thread-like element may also have supplied the sound.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The earliest form shows a foot held back by a thread-like element, expressing lagging behind; some analyses treat the thread-like element as phonetic.
stages.stageExplanation: An early delayed/lagging movement graph underlies the “behind/after” word; exact cord/foot details vary by analysis.
stages.transitionNote: The earliest form shows a foot held back by a thread-like element, expressing lagging behind; some analyses treat the thread-like element as phonetic.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Adds a clear walking-side stroke at the left while the central twisted thread and lower foot-like element remain distinct.
stages.stageExplanation: Adds a clear walking-side stroke at the left while the central twisted thread and lower foot-like element remain distinct.
stages.transitionNote: Adds a clear walking-side stroke at the left while the central twisted thread and lower foot-like element remain distinct.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Organizes the left walking component and the stacked central/lower movement marks into a tall, balanced form.
stages.stageExplanation: Organizes the left walking component and the stacked central/lower movement marks into a tall, balanced form.
stages.transitionNote: Organizes the left walking component and the stacked central/lower movement marks into a tall, balanced form.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Shortens the curves and squares the interior, bringing the structure very close to traditional.
stages.stageExplanation: Shortens the curves and squares the interior, bringing the structure very close to traditional.
stages.transitionNote: Shortens the curves and squares the interior, bringing the structure very close to traditional.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Traditional 後 preserves the historical after/behind graph. Mainland 后 is a later simplification/merger with a historically different character.
stages.stageExplanation: Traditional 後 preserves the historical after/behind graph. Mainland 后 is a later simplification/merger with a historically different character.
stages.transitionNote: Traditional 後 preserves the historical after/behind graph. Mainland 后 is a later simplification/merger with a historically different character.

origin.explanation: An early graph shows delayed or lagging movement; a walking/path component is added later in the traditional form.

history.originAnchor: The earliest form shows a mouth with a separate speech marker; later forms became more tongue-like.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A mouth and added marker indicate an utterance; the tongue-shaped form belongs to later developments.
stages.stageExplanation: A speech/tongue-related form with an added mark indicates utterance; the early graph is more specific than a generic mouth box.
stages.transitionNote: A mouth and added marker indicate an utterance; the tongue-shaped form belongs to later developments.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Bronze forms develop a tongue-like upper part and add a short horizontal marker above it, making the speech structure more explicit.
stages.stageExplanation: Thickens the upper point into a forked or hourglass-like shape while preserving the mouth below.
stages.transitionNote: Bronze forms develop a tongue-like upper part and add a short horizontal marker above it, making the speech structure more explicit.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Regularizes the stack into a short top line, a central vertical-cross structure, and a rounded mouth/opening sign at the base.
stages.stageExplanation: Regularizes the stack into a short top line, a central vertical-cross structure, and a rounded mouth/opening sign at the base.
stages.transitionNote: Regularizes the stack into a short top line, a central vertical-cross structure, and a rounded mouth/opening sign at the base.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Squares the lower mouth and flattens the upper strokes into several strong horizontals.
stages.stageExplanation: Squares the lower mouth and flattens the upper strokes into several strong horizontals.
stages.transitionNote: Squares the lower mouth and flattens the upper strokes into several strong horizontals.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The mouth-and-speech-marker structure is heavily regularized into the modern form.
stages.stageExplanation: Tightens the entire stack into the familiar top mark, horizontal lines, and 口, with the original mouth still plainly preserved at the bottom.
stages.transitionNote: The mouth-and-speech-marker structure is heavily regularized into the modern form.

history.originAnchor: A hand and a piece of meat combine to show a ritual offering; presenting it in worship led to the meaning “sacrifice.”

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The earliest core is a hand with a meat offering, often with liquid/blood/juice marks; ritual-tablet sign is not required in every early form.
stages.stageExplanation: The earliest core is a hand with a meat offering, often with liquid/blood/juice marks; ritual-tablet sign is not required in every early form.
stages.transitionNote: The earliest core is a hand with a meat offering, often with liquid/blood/juice marks; ritual-tablet sign is not required in every early form.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Later forms may add or clarify ritual material including ritual-tablet sign; describe the selected exemplar rather than assuming an altar was always present.
stages.stageExplanation: Later forms may add or clarify ritual material including ritual-tablet sign; describe the selected exemplar rather than assuming an altar was always present.
stages.transitionNote: Later forms may add or clarify ritual material including ritual-tablet sign; describe the selected exemplar rather than assuming an altar was always present.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Reorganizes the offering and hand into smooth upper curves above a tall, symmetric altar base.
stages.stageExplanation: Reorganizes the offering and hand into smooth upper curves above a tall, symmetric altar base.
stages.transitionNote: Reorganizes the offering and hand into smooth upper curves above a tall, symmetric altar base.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Flattens the upper hand/offering into angular strokes and turns the altar into the familiar ritual-tablet sign-like lower section.
stages.stageExplanation: Flattens the upper hand/offering into angular strokes and turns the altar into the familiar ritual-tablet sign-like lower section.
stages.transitionNote: Flattens the upper hand/offering into angular strokes and turns the altar into the familiar ritual-tablet sign-like lower section.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The hand/offering graph is standardized with the ritual 示-derived lower element in 祭; incense is never an encoded component.
stages.stageExplanation: The hand/offering graph is standardized with the ritual 示-derived lower element in 祭; incense is never an encoded component.
stages.transitionNote: The hand/offering graph is standardized with the ritual 示-derived lower element in 祭; incense is never an encoded component.

history.originAnchor: A person and a separate eye show looking into the distance; this led to waiting and hope, while later forms added the moon.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A standing person with an emphasized eye looks into the distance. This precedes the later reorganization of the graph and the addition or replacement of sound-bearing and lunar elements.
stages.stageExplanation: A standing person with an emphasized eye looks into the distance. This precedes the later reorganization of the graph and the addition or replacement of sound-bearing and lunar elements.
stages.transitionNote: A standing person with an emphasized eye looks into the distance. This precedes the later reorganization of the graph and the addition or replacement of sound-bearing and lunar elements.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Later forms reorganize the looking graph; sound-bearing element functions phonetically in the developing lineage, while moon sign belongs to moon/lunar-phase-related variants rather than a simple “moon-gazing” origin.
stages.stageExplanation: Later forms reorganize the looking graph; sound-bearing element functions phonetically in the developing lineage, while moon sign belongs to moon/lunar-phase-related variants rather than a simple “moon-gazing” origin.
stages.transitionNote: Later forms reorganize the looking graph; sound-bearing element functions phonetically in the developing lineage, while moon sign belongs to moon/lunar-phase-related variants rather than a simple “moon-gazing” origin.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Integrates the left standing figure and right eye/moon into a tall, tightly interlocked structure.
stages.stageExplanation: Integrates the left standing figure and right eye/moon into a tall, tightly interlocked structure.
stages.transitionNote: Integrates the left standing figure and right eye/moon into a tall, tightly interlocked structure.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Flattens the upper parts and creates the recognizable stacked moon sign/king form-like right side over a long base.
stages.stageExplanation: Flattens the upper parts and creates the recognizable stacked moon sign/king form-like right side over a long base.
stages.transitionNote: Flattens the upper parts and creates the recognizable stacked moon sign/king form-like right side over a long base.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The regular 望 structure reflects later phonetic/component history; the original act of looking afar is no longer directly pictorial.
stages.stageExplanation: The regular 望 structure reflects later phonetic/component history; the original act of looking afar is no longer directly pictorial.
stages.transitionNote: The regular 望 structure reflects later phonetic/component history; the original act of looking afar is no longer directly pictorial.

recognitionTakeaway: The graph specializes as 冬 for winter, while 終 later preserves the general “end” sense with an added silk component.
visualTeachingNotes: A person moving across ice, with a weak winter sun and frozen blocks shown below.
Oracle is simply a broad arch with hooked ends; it does not resemble snow, ice, or the modern character in any obvious way.
Regular 冬 reduces the old complexity to the descending 夂-like top and two small lower dots, a very compact endpoint compared with the intermediate forms.

history.originAnchor: A cord tied at both ends suggests an ending. The winter sense developed later from the end of the yearly cycle, not by a simple sound borrowing.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The early cord-like form represents an ending in the leading analysis; the lower marks are not yet secure ice signs.
stages.stageExplanation: A cord/string with tied ends represents an ending in the leading analysis; the later lower dots are not primordial ice marks.
stages.transitionNote: The early cord-like form represents an ending in the leading analysis; the lower marks are not yet secure ice signs.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Adds a small roofed or enclosed shape above a long vertical and horizontal line, creating a much more structured sign.
stages.stageExplanation: Adds a small roofed or enclosed shape above a long vertical and horizontal line, creating a much more structured sign.
stages.transitionNote: Adds a small roofed or enclosed shape above a long vertical and horizontal line, creating a much more structured sign.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Replaces that arrangement with a capped upper enclosure over two pairs of downward strokes.
stages.stageExplanation: Replaces that arrangement with a capped upper enclosure over two pairs of downward strokes.
stages.transitionNote: Replaces that arrangement with a capped upper enclosure over two pairs of downward strokes.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Compresses the lower marks into two sweeping diagonals and a short center, bringing the form close to winter form.
stages.stageExplanation: Compresses the lower marks into two sweeping diagonals and a short center, bringing the form close to winter form.
stages.transitionNote: Compresses the lower marks into two sweeping diagonals and a short center, bringing the form close to winter form.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The graph became the dedicated sign for winter, while the general ending sense was written separately with a silk-related addition.
stages.stageExplanation: The graph specializes as 冬 for winter, while 終 later preserves the general “end” sense with an added silk component.
stages.transitionNote: The graph became the dedicated sign for winter, while the general ending sense was written separately with a silk-related addition.

origin.explanation: A cord/string with tied ends, representing an ending/termination in a leading account.

history.originAnchor: Leading theory: a person receiving facial tattooing and dark pigment as punishment; the sign later meant 'black,' inspiring a fire-and-chimney explanation.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A leading account reads the early form as a human/head with a dark facial mark; this interpretation is disputed and should be illustrated non-graphically.
stages.stageExplanation: A leading account reads the early form as a human/head with a dark facial mark; this interpretation is disputed and should be illustrated non-graphically.
stages.transitionNote: A leading account reads the early form as a human/head with a dark facial mark; this interpretation is disputed and should be illustrated non-graphically.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Keeps the upright person silhouette but makes the head a pointed dark enclosure with paired internal marks.
stages.stageExplanation: Keeps the upright person silhouette but makes the head a pointed dark enclosure with paired internal marks.
stages.transitionNote: Keeps the upright person silhouette but makes the head a pointed dark enclosure with paired internal marks.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Expands the head into a broad barred top and adds several long downward strokes beneath, producing a much more complex figure.
stages.stageExplanation: Expands the head into a broad barred top and adds several long downward strokes beneath, producing a much more complex figure.
stages.transitionNote: Expands the head into a broad barred top and adds several long downward strokes beneath, producing a much more complex figure.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The broad upper section flattens and the lower strokes condense into a dense spread, closely anticipating the later standard structure.
stages.stageExplanation: The broad upper section flattens and the lower strokes condense into a dense spread, closely anticipating the later standard structure.
stages.transitionNote: The broad upper section flattens and the lower strokes condense into a dense spread, closely anticipating the later standard structure.

stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The penal-tattoo graph came to write ‘black’ and displaced an older color term; the later soot-and-chimney explanation is a reinterpretation, not the original picture.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: One early form resembles a nest or container; another may be a different borrowed form. The sunset explanation is traditional but disputed.
stages.stageExplanation: A nest/container-like object is the pictorial source in a leading analysis; it should not be expanded into a sunset scene.
stages.transitionNote: One early form resembles a nest or container; another may be a different borrowed form. The sunset explanation is traditional but disputed.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Simplifies the enclosure into a pointed oval or pouch with a strong X-like crossing inside.
stages.stageExplanation: Simplifies the enclosure into a pointed oval or pouch with a strong X-like crossing inside.
stages.transitionNote: Simplifies the enclosure into a pointed oval or pouch with a strong X-like crossing inside.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Adds a long curved top and places the crossed enclosure below it, creating a more organized two-part structure.
stages.stageExplanation: Adds a long curved top and places the crossed enclosure below it, creating a more organized two-part structure.
stages.transitionNote: Adds a long curved top and places the crossed enclosure below it, creating a more organized two-part structure.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Flattens the outer shape into a wide box with four small inner compartments and a long top stroke.

stages.transitionNote: Flattens the outer shape into a wide box with four small inner compartments and a long top stroke.

recognitionTakeaway: 申 survives with later state/apply/extend-related uses, while 電 adds 雨 for lightning/electricity and 伸 adds 人 for stretching.
visualTeachingNotes: A twisting, lightning-like line stretched out beside a person pulling on a long cord.
Oracle is a loose S-shaped sequence of two opposing curls, with no enclosing frame and no obvious modern rectangle.
Regular 申 encloses the central vertical inside a rectangular 日-like frame, a major final restructuring from the open Seal and Clerical forms.

history.originAnchor: A roof and a hand combine to show guarding what lies beneath; this led to 'protect.'

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A roofed dwelling combines with a hand/action element, forming the concrete guarding/keeping relation.
stages.stageExplanation: A roofed dwelling combines with a hand/action element, forming the concrete guarding/keeping relation.
stages.transitionNote: A roofed dwelling combines with a hand/action element, forming the concrete guarding/keeping relation.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Lowers the roof into a rounded arch and makes the inner guarding form a broad curled stroke.
stages.stageExplanation: Lowers the roof into a rounded arch and makes the inner guarding form a broad curled stroke.
stages.transitionNote: Lowers the roof into a rounded arch and makes the inner guarding form a broad curled stroke.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Restores a tall house-like enclosure and centers several short hand-like strokes inside it.
stages.stageExplanation: Restores a tall house-like enclosure and centers several short hand-like strokes inside it.
stages.transitionNote: Restores a tall house-like enclosure and centers several short hand-like strokes inside it.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The roof is flattened and the enclosed hand/action element becomes compact and angular, approaching the later standard arrangement.
stages.stageExplanation: The roof is flattened and the enclosed hand/action element becomes compact and angular, approaching the later standard arrangement.
stages.transitionNote: The roof is flattened and the enclosed hand/action element becomes compact and angular, approaching the later standard arrangement.

visualTeachingNotes: A group of people gathered under a flag, with a spear or weapon shown as part of the scene.
Oracle shows a tall flagpole or banner beside a small human or weapon-like figure, with the components still widely separated.
Regular 族 standardizes 方 on the left and the compact arrow/person-derived right side, preserving the sense of a group organized under a banner only through its components.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A banner/standard combines with an arrow/weapon element, reflecting organized social/military grouping.
stages.stageExplanation: A banner/standard combines with an arrow/weapon element, reflecting organized social/military grouping.
stages.transitionNote: A banner/standard combines with an arrow/weapon element, reflecting organized social/military grouping.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Makes the banner into a strong vertical-and-horizontal frame and places a clear person-like figure beneath or inside it.
stages.stageExplanation: Makes the banner into a strong vertical-and-horizontal frame and places a clear person-like figure beneath or inside it.
stages.transitionNote: Makes the banner into a strong vertical-and-horizontal frame and places a clear person-like figure beneath or inside it.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Develops a tall left banner component beside a structured right section with several vertical strokes.
stages.stageExplanation: Develops a tall left banner component beside a structured right section with several vertical strokes.
stages.transitionNote: Develops a tall left banner component beside a structured right section with several vertical strokes.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Flattens both halves into a dense form that is already close to clan form.
stages.stageExplanation: Flattens both halves into a dense form that is already close to clan form.
stages.transitionNote: Flattens both halves into a dense form that is already close to clan form.

recognitionTakeaway: The troop/expedition graph becomes 旅 and extends to journey/travel.

recognitionTakeaway: The graph stabilizes as 古 for “old/ancient”; the folk “ten mouths tell old stories” account is excluded.
visualTeachingNotes: A round shield-like object and an open mouth shown combining into an old stone chamber or structure.
Oracle places a cross-marked upper shape over a large open mouth-like enclosure, already forming a clear top-and-bottom compound.
Regular 古 tightens 十 over 口 into the familiar six-stroke character, with the original pictorial interpretation no longer obvious.

recognitionTakeaway: The compound stabilizes as 妻; V2 avoids presenting bride capture as an established pictorial fact.
visualTeachingNotes: A woman having her long hair gathered or arranged by a hand, with a broom-like object shown nearby.
Oracle is a dense human figure with branching hair or hand strokes at the top and a long woman-like body below.
Regular 妻 fixes the stacked upper strokes over 女, preserving the two-level figure while removing the literal hair-arranging scene.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A bound set of writing slips is placed on a broad support; the lower form is the stand, not a pair of presenting hands.
stages.stageExplanation: A bound set of writing slips is placed on a broad support; the lower form is the stand, not a pair of presenting hands.
stages.transitionNote: A bound set of writing slips is placed on a broad support; the lower form is the stand, not a pair of presenting hands.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Makes the bound-slip grid clearer and separates it from the broad lower support.
stages.stageExplanation: Makes the bound-slip grid clearer and separates it from the broad lower support.
stages.transitionNote: Makes the bound-slip grid clearer and separates it from the broad lower support.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Regularizes the slips into a neat lattice standing on two long legs or supports.
stages.stageExplanation: Regularizes the slips into a neat lattice standing on two long legs or supports.
stages.transitionNote: Regularizes the slips into a neat lattice standing on two long legs or supports.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书

stages.transitionNote: Thickens the lattice and adds a distinct small lower mark beneath the support.

history.originAnchor: Two human figures stand back-to-back, expressing the earlier idea of ‘back.’

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Two human figures stand back-to-back, directly expressing the old “back/back-facing” idea.
stages.stageExplanation: Two human figures stand back-to-back, directly expressing the old “back/back-facing” idea.
stages.transitionNote: Two human figures stand back-to-back, directly expressing the old “back/back-facing” idea.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Reduces the pair to two thick mirrored figures with inward-facing straight edges and outward-curving backs.
stages.stageExplanation: Reduces the pair to two thick mirrored figures with inward-facing straight edges and outward-curving backs.
stages.transitionNote: Reduces the pair to two thick mirrored figures with inward-facing straight edges and outward-curving backs.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Stretches them into two tall, narrow mirrored curves separated by a clear central gap.
stages.stageExplanation: Stretches them into two tall, narrow mirrored curves separated by a clear central gap.
stages.transitionNote: Stretches them into two tall, narrow mirrored curves separated by a clear central gap.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Shortens and thickens both halves, preserving the back-to-back opposition more clearly than the Seal form.
stages.stageExplanation: Shortens and thickens both halves, preserving the back-to-back opposition more clearly than the Seal form.
stages.transitionNote: Shortens and thickens both halves, preserving the back-to-back opposition more clearly than the Seal form.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The back-to-back graph was later borrowed by sound for ‘north’; the ordinary ‘back’ sense came to be written with a body-related addition.
stages.stageExplanation: The back-to-back graph stabilizes as 北 for “north,” while 背 later carries the ordinary “back” sense.
stages.transitionNote: The back-to-back graph was later borrowed by sound for ‘north’; the ordinary ‘back’ sense came to be written with a body-related addition.

history.originAnchor: The early picture is disputed: a person in a neck restraint is one leading interpretation. The graph was later borrowed by sound for ‘center.’

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A front-facing person carries an element centered around the neck or shoulders. A neck restraint is one leading interpretation, but the ancient scene remains disputed.
stages.stageExplanation: A front-facing person carries an element centered around the neck or shoulders. The exact ancient scene is debated internally, but the central placement is visually clear.
stages.transitionNote: A front-facing person carries an element centered around the neck or shoulders. A neck restraint is one leading interpretation, but the ancient scene remains disputed.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The human body and centered crosspiece become more compact and integrated.
stages.stageExplanation: The human body and centered crosspiece become more compact and integrated.
stages.transitionNote: The human body and centered crosspiece become more compact and integrated.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The earlier human scene is heavily regularized into a balanced written structure; much of the original anatomy is no longer obvious.
stages.stageExplanation: The earlier human scene is heavily regularized into a balanced written structure; much of the original anatomy is no longer obvious.
stages.transitionNote: The earlier human scene is heavily regularized into a balanced written structure; much of the original anatomy is no longer obvious.

stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The Seal curves flatten into the angular skeleton that leads directly to the standard form.

stages.label: Regular Script

recognitionTakeaway: A human nose; traditionally, pointing to one’s own nose was a familiar way to refer to oneself, helping this nose symbol develop the meaning “self.” As that meaning became dominant, another written representation took over the specific meaning “nose.”
visualTeachingNotes: A person pointing to or touching the nose on their own face.
A broad nose-like outline encloses one strong internal horizontal, with two lower side lobes hanging beneath.
Regular 自 squares the outline, keeps the interior horizontals, and turns the split top into the small opening stroke of the modern character.

history.originAnchor: A nose is the pictorial source. The meaning ‘self’ was later borrowed by sound; the nose-pointing explanation is a later folk interpretation.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The early form is a nose pictograph; it does not yet depict the abstract idea ‘self.’
stages.stageExplanation: The graph is a nose pictograph with internal structural detail; the later “self” sense should not be acted out inside the origin image.
stages.transitionNote: The early form is a nose pictograph; it does not yet depict the abstract idea ‘self.’

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The outline becomes more symmetrical and fills with several stacked horizontal bands.
stages.stageExplanation: The outline becomes more symmetrical and fills with several stacked horizontal bands.
stages.transitionNote: The outline becomes more symmetrical and fills with several stacked horizontal bands.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The form is organized into a tall rounded enclosure with a split top and two clear interior lines.
stages.stageExplanation: The form is organized into a tall rounded enclosure with a split top and two clear interior lines.
stages.transitionNote: The form is organized into a tall rounded enclosure with a split top and two clear interior lines.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The same structure is thickened into a dense box-like nose shape.
stages.stageExplanation: The same structure is thickened into a dense box-like nose shape.
stages.transitionNote: The same structure is thickened into a dense box-like nose shape.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The nose graph was later used for ‘self’ by sound, so a body-related addition was introduced for the ordinary nose sense.
stages.stageExplanation: The old nose picture becomes the regular graph 自. Because 自 had taken over the “self” word, 鼻 later carries the ordinary nose sense.
stages.transitionNote: The nose graph was later used for ‘self’ by sound, so a body-related addition was introduced for the ordinary nose sense.

origin.explanation: The graph originally depicted a nose.

history.originAnchor: A tongue projecting from an open mouth.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The earliest form shows a mouth with a forked tongue; later variants add a base stroke and sometimes extra dots or a stone-like element.
stages.stageExplanation: A mouth-like box sits at the bottom while a central tongue rises above it and splits into small upper strokes.
stages.transitionNote: The earliest form shows a mouth with a forked tongue; later variants add a base stroke and sometimes extra dots or a stone-like element.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Bronze forms standardize the double-forked tongue and add four dots between it and the mouth.
stages.stageExplanation: The tongue becomes taller and more symmetrical, with paired side marks and a clearer mouth enclosure below.
stages.transitionNote: Bronze forms standardize the double-forked tongue and add four dots between it and the mouth.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The parts align on a central axis: a forked top, long stem, crossbar, and rounded mouth at the bottom.
stages.stageExplanation: The parts align on a central axis: a forked top, long stem, crossbar, and rounded mouth at the bottom.
stages.transitionNote: The parts align on a central axis: a forked top, long stem, crossbar, and rounded mouth at the bottom.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The added dots disappear in later forms, leaving the simpler tongue-over-mouth structure that leads to the modern form.
stages.stageExplanation: The forked upper strokes spread into a brushy cross while the lower mouth becomes a heavy rectangular bowl.
stages.transitionNote: The added dots disappear in later forms, leaving the simpler tongue-over-mouth structure that leads to the modern form.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Simplifies the upper fork into a short top stroke over 十, while the mouth remains as 口 at the bottom.
stages.stageExplanation: Simplifies the upper fork into a short top stroke over 十, while the mouth remains as 口 at the bottom.
stages.transitionNote: Simplifies the upper fork into a short top stroke over 十, while the mouth remains as 口 at the bottom.

Regular 女 condenses those crossing curves into three strokes, preserving the bent, crossed posture in a highly abstract form.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: An upper mark associated with the sky sits above a curling lower element. The lower element mainly carries the sound in the leading analysis, while the complete graph is used for “cloud.”

stages.transitionNote: The upper and curling lower elements become more compact and regular, while the cloud word continues to use the same basic graph.

history.originAnchor: Rain falling from the sky.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A long upper line and several hanging strokes suggest rain beneath a sky or cloud, but without the meaning it is not immediately recognizable as rain.
stages.stageExplanation: A long upper line and several hanging strokes suggest rain beneath a sky or cloud, but without the meaning it is not immediately recognizable as rain.
stages.transitionNote: A long upper line and several hanging strokes suggest rain beneath a sky or cloud, but without the meaning it is not immediately recognizable as rain.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The form becomes a heavy rectangular frame with paired vertical openings, keeping the hanging-stroke idea but looking more architectural than meteorological.
stages.stageExplanation: The form becomes a heavy rectangular frame with paired vertical openings, keeping the hanging-stroke idea but looking more architectural than meteorological.
stages.transitionNote: The form becomes a heavy rectangular frame with paired vertical openings, keeping the hanging-stroke idea but looking more architectural than meteorological.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A complete outer frame and central divider appear, with four small interior marks arranged in pairs; standardization makes the form more complex, not more pictorial.
stages.stageExplanation: A complete outer frame and central divider appear, with four small interior marks arranged in pairs; standardization makes the form more complex, not more pictorial.
stages.transitionNote: A complete outer frame and central divider appear, with four small interior marks arranged in pairs; standardization makes the form more complex, not more pictorial.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The Seal frame is flattened and opened into broad clerical strokes; some interior lines merge while the four small marks remain as short horizontal elements.
stages.stageExplanation: The Seal frame is flattened and opened into broad clerical strokes; some interior lines merge while the four small marks remain as short horizontal elements.
stages.transitionNote: The Seal frame is flattened and opened into broad clerical strokes; some interior lines merge while the four small marks remain as short horizontal elements.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A top line was added after the earliest forms; later regularization keeps it above four drop marks.
stages.stageExplanation: Restores a clear top line and turns the four interior marks into diagonal dots, making them look more like falling drops again than in several intermediate stages.
stages.transitionNote: A top line was added after the earliest forms; later regularization keeps it above four drop marks.

visualTeachingNotes: A loose stone beside a rocky cliff face.
A slanted outer stroke forms a cliff-like edge with a small enclosed opening inside; the stone is not a simple round boulder here.
Regular 石 regularizes the cliff into the top-left strokes and the stone into a square 口-like lower component.

stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The earliest selected form is angular and object-like, preserving the outline of a resonant stone or stone-chime form rather than a simple loose rock.

history.originAnchor: A framed well opening, showing a protected source of water.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A square well mouth/framework is crossed by wooden rails; small central details vary by exemplar.
stages.stageExplanation: A square well mouth/framework is crossed by wooden rails; small central details vary by exemplar.
stages.transitionNote: A square well mouth/framework is crossed by wooden rails; small central details vary by exemplar.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The same frame becomes straighter, with two strong horizontals crossing two vertical supports.
stages.stageExplanation: The same frame becomes straighter, with two strong horizontals crossing two vertical supports.
stages.transitionNote: The same frame becomes straighter, with two strong horizontals crossing two vertical supports.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The frame is drawn tall and narrow, and a small dot appears near the center of the selected Seal form.
stages.stageExplanation: The frame is drawn tall and narrow, and a small dot appears near the center of the selected Seal form.
stages.transitionNote: The frame is drawn tall and narrow, and a small dot appears near the center of the selected Seal form.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The dot disappears and the crossed rails thicken into a compact, brushy grid.
stages.stageExplanation: The dot disappears and the crossed rails thicken into a compact, brushy grid.
stages.transitionNote: The dot disappears and the crossed rails thicken into a compact, brushy grid.

stages.label: Regular Script

stages.transitionNote: The intersecting frame is regularized as 井, preserving the old well-mouth geometry.

recognitionTakeaway: The lodging graph stabilizes as 宿, with roof + person/resting-material compressed into a conventional structure.
visualTeachingNotes: A person lying down to sleep beneath a roof or simple shelter.
Oracle shows a pointed roof enclosing a bent person-like figure or sleeping body on one side.
Regular 宿 standardizes 宀 over the person-and-bed derived lower components; the scene of sleeping under a roof is no longer literal but the shelter structure remains clear.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: A person rests on a mat; roof/shelter appears in expanded forms and should not erase the mat from the origin explanation.

stages.transitionNote: Makes the shelter large and rounded and encloses a much clearer curled body and bedding-like shapes inside.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文

stages.label: Bronze / 金文

stages.transitionNote: The head becomes a heavy cap atop a simplified standing body, while the limbs remain visible.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆

stages.transitionNote: Connects the idea into a more organized shape: three upright strokes sit above a long sweeping lower line.

stages.transitionNote: Keeps the three upper strokes but bends the lower stroke into a strong curved tail.

stages.transitionNote: Turns the upper strokes into three compact dots and broadens the lower sweep.

recognitionTakeaway: 中 standardizes the enclosure and central line; the modern geometry preserves the idea of a visibly marked center.
visualTeachingNotes: A central pole or marker placed through the middle of a larger object, shown as the idea of a center.
Oracle has a vertical pole passing through a rounded central shape, with several loose streamers or side strokes extending from it.
Regular 中 squares the enclosure and extends the central vertical cleanly through it, making the “through the middle” relation visually obvious again.

history.originAnchor: The longer line marks a boundary or reference level; the short mark below points to the space below. This abstract sign came to mean 'below'.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Uses a long upper line with a shorter mark clearly placed underneath it.
stages.stageExplanation: Uses a long upper line with a shorter mark clearly placed underneath it.
stages.transitionNote: Uses a long upper line with a shorter mark clearly placed underneath it.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Repeats the same two-level relation with straighter, heavier strokes.
stages.stageExplanation: Repeats the same two-level relation with straighter, heavier strokes.
stages.transitionNote: Repeats the same two-level relation with straighter, heavier strokes.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Joins the idea into one form by dropping a vertical line down from the long top horizontal.
stages.stageExplanation: Joins the idea into one form by dropping a vertical line down from the long top horizontal.
stages.transitionNote: Joins the idea into one form by dropping a vertical line down from the long top horizontal.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Retains the top bar and hanging vertical, adding a small separated side stroke.
stages.stageExplanation: Retains the top bar and hanging vertical, adding a small separated side stroke.
stages.transitionNote: Retains the top bar and hanging vertical, adding a small separated side stroke.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The original mark below a line was later reshaped with a vertical stroke to distinguish it from the numeral for two; the meaning ‘below’ remained.
stages.stageExplanation: Stabilizes the top horizontal, central descending stroke, and short diagonal side mark into the modern form.
stages.transitionNote: The original mark below a line was later reshaped with a vertical stroke to distinguish it from the numeral for two; the meaning ‘below’ remained.

history.originAnchor: The longer line marks a boundary or the ground; the short mark above points to the space above. This abstract sign came to mean 'above'.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Expresses the idea directly with a short horizontal floating over a longer one.
stages.stageExplanation: Expresses the idea directly with a short horizontal floating over a longer one.
stages.transitionNote: Expresses the idea directly with a short horizontal floating over a longer one.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Preserves the two-level arrangement but exaggerates the thickness and tilt of both bars.
stages.stageExplanation: Preserves the two-level arrangement but exaggerates the thickness and tilt of both bars.
stages.transitionNote: Preserves the two-level arrangement but exaggerates the thickness and tilt of both bars.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Changes the logic: a vertical now rises from a long baseline, turning the upper relation into a more integrated symbol.
stages.stageExplanation: Changes the logic: a vertical now rises from a long baseline, turning the upper relation into a more integrated symbol.
stages.transitionNote: Changes the logic: a vertical now rises from a long baseline, turning the upper relation into a more integrated symbol.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Keeps the upright-on-baseline shape with heavier, flatter brush strokes.
stages.stageExplanation: Keeps the upright-on-baseline shape with heavier, flatter brush strokes.
stages.transitionNote: Keeps the upright-on-baseline shape with heavier, flatter brush strokes.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The original mark above a line was later reshaped with a vertical stroke to distinguish it from the numeral for two; the meaning ‘above’ remained.
stages.stageExplanation: Adds the short upper horizontal to the vertical stem while retaining the long lower baseline.
stages.transitionNote: The original mark above a line was later reshaped with a vertical stroke to distinguish it from the numeral for two; the meaning ‘above’ remained.

recognitionTakeaway: Traditional 長 regularizes the old elder figure; Simplified Chinese later uses 长.
visualTeachingNotes: An elderly person with very long hair, shown beside a hanging lock of hair and a cane.
A side-facing figure carries a large rectangular upper mass with long trailing strokes below, emphasizing length through the extended body or hair.
Modern simplified 长 removes most of the internal structure of 長, leaving a much more open four-stroke form while preserving the long downward sweep.

recognitionTakeaway: The tool picture is abstracted into 力, which now directly carries strength/force meanings.
visualTeachingNotes: A person levering a heavy tool beside a curved implement and a flexed arm showing force.
Oracle is a long hooked stroke with a small crossing branch near the lower end, more tool-like than muscular.
Regular 力 tightens the hook and long diagonal into two principal strokes, preserving the sense of a bent, exerting form.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文

recognitionTakeaway: A bladed working tool, used for working the ground or making boundaries. Some scholars instead see a carpenter’s square for measuring and marking, so the exact tool is uncertain; the character later came to mean “work” or “craft.”
visualTeachingNotes: A handled digging tool beside a person working the ground and a simple carpentry joint.
Oracle looks like a T-shaped handle planted into a rounded rectangular working end.
Regular 工 keeps exactly that three-stroke framework, with only brush taper distinguishing it from the geometric Seal form.

recognitionTakeaway: This picture shows a high-footed lidded vessel, not a bean. The vessel’s name sounded like the word for beans, so its picture was borrowed to write that word; this sound-based meaning became dominant, while the vessel meaning survived mainly in historical contexts.
visualTeachingNotes: A lidded pedestal vessel—the object depicted by the old pictograph, rather than a modern bean.
Oracle clearly shows a bowl or vessel resting on a narrow stand and broad foot.
Regular 豆 preserves the stacked vessel structure as a top lid, central container, narrow support, and bottom strokes even though the everyday meaning later shifted to “bean.”

history.originAnchor: A sheep or ram head with curved horns.

stages.label: Oracle Bone / 甲骨文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Two pointed horn shapes rise from a central vertical and the lower end forks sharply, giving the form a strong animal-head symmetry.
stages.stageExplanation: Two pointed horn shapes rise from a central vertical and the lower end forks sharply, giving the form a strong animal-head symmetry.
stages.transitionNote: Two pointed horn shapes rise from a central vertical and the lower end forks sharply, giving the form a strong animal-head symmetry.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The horns simplify into a wide angular fork while the lower point becomes an arrow-like split.
stages.stageExplanation: The horns simplify into a wide angular fork while the lower point becomes an arrow-like split.
stages.transitionNote: The horns simplify into a wide angular fork while the lower point becomes an arrow-like split.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Several horizontal lines are added across the central stem, producing a form already recognizably close to sheep sign.
stages.stageExplanation: Several horizontal lines are added across the central stem, producing a form already recognizably close to sheep sign.
stages.transitionNote: Several horizontal lines are added across the central stem, producing a form already recognizably close to sheep sign.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The horn tips and stacked horizontals are retained but flattened and thickened by clerical brushwork.
stages.stageExplanation: The horn tips and stacked horizontals are retained but flattened and thickened by clerical brushwork.
stages.transitionNote: The horn tips and stacked horizontals are retained but flattened and thickened by clerical brushwork.

stages.label: Regular Script
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Regularizes the paired top strokes, three horizontals, and central vertical into the familiar modern form.
stages.stageExplanation: Regularizes the paired top strokes, three horizontals, and central vertical into the familiar modern form.

stages.label: Bronze / 金文
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: Becomes highly pictorial again: broad horns, forehead, eyes, muzzle, and face are all clearly visible.
stages.stageExplanation: Becomes highly pictorial again: broad horns, forehead, eyes, muzzle, and face are all clearly visible.
stages.transitionNote: Becomes highly pictorial again: broad horns, forehead, eyes, muzzle, and face are all clearly visible.

stages.label: Small Seal / 小篆
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The animal head is radically abstracted into a forked top, central vertical, and one strong horizontal crossbar.
stages.stageExplanation: The animal head is radically abstracted into a forked top, central vertical, and one strong horizontal crossbar.
stages.transitionNote: The animal head is radically abstracted into a forked top, central vertical, and one strong horizontal crossbar.

stages.label: Clerical / 隶书
stages.changeNoteFromPrevious: The same skeleton thickens into broad clerical strokes, with the horn fork and crossbar still obvious.
stages.stageExplanation: The same skeleton thickens into broad clerical strokes, with the horn fork and crossbar still obvious.
stages.transitionNote: The same skeleton thickens into broad clerical strokes, with the horn fork and crossbar still obvious.

recognitionTakeaway: The modern 祝 structure preserves the ritual semantic component 礻 beside the speaking/person-derived right side; no incense belongs to the graph.
visualTeachingNotes: A person kneeling in prayer beside an offering altar with incense rising from it.
Oracle places a clear 示-like altar on the left and a tall kneeling or speaking human form on the right.
Regular 祝 fixes 礻 on the left and 兄 on the right, preserving the ritual scene as the combination of an altar and a person addressing or praying before it.
